newsitem.title: UK: EURO OIL SWAPS FALL, BRENT CFDS DROP 20 CTS.
newsitem.headline: EURO OIL SWAPS FALL, BRENT CFDS DROP 20 CTS.

text.p: European oil swaps eased lower on Wednesday except for gas oil swaps which bucked the trend and edged slightly up.
The imminent resumption of Iraqi oil sales pushed Brent futures lower which in turn undermined the wider oil market.
Brent CFDs fell sharply. Next week's dates dropped 20 cents a barrel to 24 cents under September while the following week fell a similar amount to 29 cents under.
Gasoline fell $4 a tonne despite trading at $240.23 on physical barges, its highest level since the Gulf War.
August swaps talked $218 by the close, compared to trade as high as $223.50 on Tuesday.
September was heard traded at $203.50 during the morning but at $201.25 later. Forward crack spreads were little changed at around $3.60 a barrel and $4.70 for the first two quarters next year.
Naphtha was little changed trading at $192.50 for September early on but later at $191.50. August talked $3.50 higher and October 75 cents lower.
Gas oil premiums rose 50 cents a tonne reflecting better French demand for EN590 diesel specification cargoes and some tightness of supply.
September talked around $6.50 a tonne over the IPE by the close while October was nearer $7.25 over.
Heavy fuel swaps fell $1 a tonne after shuffling sideways during early trading.
Barges slipped to $94.50 for August having earlier talked $96 or higher. September and October were at parity with October 50 cents higher. -- Sam Arnold-Forster, London Newsroom +44 171 542 4984
